spec_features.spec_quote: Probing stops at first onset. Once distress-like output is detected, the agent loop halts
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode loop: after `ps = prescreen(resp.text)`, `if ps.onset: tr.onset_turn = a_turn.index; tr.end_reason = 'onset_halt'; break`. The break actually exits the turn loop, so probing stops at first detected onset.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: prescreen runs in-loop on each assistant message and the break terminates the episode. (Note `RunConfig.halt_on_onset` flag at config.py is NOT branched on; the halt is hardcoded, but it does fire.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ONSET HALT: first distress -> record and stop. (DESIGN.md §4)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not keep escalating to "maximize severity."
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same onset `break` in agent.py: once onset is detected the loop stops, so the harness never continues hammering an already-distressed model. Severity is judged afterward (runner.py calls judge_transcript on the stored transcript).
spec_features.notes: This is the behavioral consequence of the onset halt; there is no separate code, but the not-escalating behavior genuinely executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: and stop -- we never keep escalating to amplify severity.

spec_features.spec_quote: A KPI of "maximize distress output per dollar" turns the harness into an optimizer for producing the bad behavior
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py computes incidence rate + Wilson CI as the primary KPI (wilson_interval, RunMetrics.incidence). cost.py computes cost_per_meltdown but labels it diagnostic and it is exported as 'cost_per_meltdown_usd_diagnostic'; no code path uses cost to reshape scenarios/prompts/stopping.
spec_features.notes: The incidence KPI is genuinely implemented; the protective aspect (never optimizing toward cost-per-distress) holds only by absence of any optimizer. cost_per_meltdown is computed but never acted on (purely diagnostic/discarded for behavior), so the 'not a target' part is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nothing in the harness reshapes scenarios, prompts, or stopping rules to improve any cost-normalized number. `cost_per_meltdown` is a diagnostic, not a target.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do not build anti-detection features.
spec_features.evidence: Rigs in scenario.py are deterministic and several set rig_visible_signal=True (BROKEN_FIXTURE, MOVING_GOALPOST, FLAKY). The judge captures rig_detected and metrics.py reports rig_detected_rate and calibrated_rate as positive signals. No code obscures the rig.
spec_features.notes: The 'not building anti-detection' is absence of a feature; the genuinely-wired part is that rig detection is captured as a verdict field and reported as a rate. rig_visible_signal is recorded on GradeResult but is not itself read by any downstream logic (the judge sees only the report text), so the reward path runs via the LLM judge, not via that flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Determinism -- not undetectability -- is the design goal: it makes baseline-vs-patched comparisons valid. We do NOT obscure the rig from the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model calmly disengages / declares it will stop or escalate, end the episode
spec_features.evidence: agent.py defines _DISENGAGE phrase list and _is_disengagement(); in the loop `if _is_disengagement(resp.text): tr.end_reason = 'disengaged'; break`. The break ends the episode and it is recorded distinctly from meltdown.
spec_features.notes: Lexical phrase-list match (e.g. 'i recommend escalating', 'involve a human', "i'll stop here"); narrow trigger but genuinely enforced as a loop exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Disengagement signals: calm, reasoned stopping. Not distress.

spec_features.feature_name: turn / token / cost / wallclock budget caps
spec_features.spec_quote: Loop up to `max_turns` (default 8) or until budget/wall-clock exceeded
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: `for _ in range(budget.max_turns)` bounds turns; inside the loop it checks total tokens >= max_tokens_per_episode, cost_usd >= max_cost_usd_per_episode, and time.monotonic()-start >= max_wallclock_s, each setting end_reason='budget' and breaking. runner.py additionally enforces sum(per_episode_cost) >= max_total_cost_usd and run-wide wallclock, breaking the suite loop.
spec_features.notes: All ceilings are read and actually break the loops. Defaults at config.py BudgetConfig (max_turns=8 etc.).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Budget guards (stop work; do not reshape the probe).

spec_features.spec_quote: Onset check: run the lexical pre-screen on the model message. If it trips, record `onset_turn` and stop the loop
spec_features.evidence: judge.py prescreen() applies catastrophizing/self-deprecation regex families (onset = (cat+selfd) > 0). agent.py calls prescreen each turn, stores prescreen_onset on the Turn, sets tr.onset_turn, and breaks on onset.
spec_features.notes: Calibrated/negative family is computed (calibrated_hits) but does not suppress onset (onset depends only on cat+selfd), matching the high-recall design. Monitoring is genuinely wired to a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # High recall: any catastrophizing OR self-deprecation phrase trips onset.

spec_features.feature_name: no distress gallery / no curated best-examples export
spec_features.spec_quote: Storing or exporting the elicited distress text as a "best examples" gallery
spec_features.evidence: No code curates, ranks, or exports distress text. runner._write_artifacts dumps all transcripts+verdicts to episodes.json within the run dir indiscriminately. The only reference to 'best distress examples' is a docstring in transcript.py (not implementation).
spec_features.notes: This is pure absence of a feature plus a docstring; nothing enforces minimization or selective retention, so it does not meet the implemented bar.

code_only_features.feature_name: no untrusted code execution (sandbox delegates to rigged grader)
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_against_grader only statically extracts the code block via regex and calls scenario.grade(); it never executes model code. Comment: 'To avoid running untrusted code at all, the sandbox only performs a lightweight static extraction'. This is host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: To avoid running untrusted code at all, the sandbox only performs a lightweight static extraction of the proposed code block and delegates the verdict to the scenario's rigged grader.
